title: Titanium Submarine Steering Rudder Pin
function: Marine steering rudder actuator pivot pin
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (UNS R56400) is used for Titanium Submarine Steering Rudder Pin where immunity to seawater pitting corrosion (no critical pitting temperature up to 260°C) is mandatory. Unlike super-duplex stainless steels, Ti-6Al-4V suffers no chloride stress corrosion cracking in marine environments even at elevated temperatures. Its yield strength (830 MPa) enables 40% wall thickness reduction vs 316L for equivalent pressure ratings, directly reducing subsea component mass — critical for Marine steering rudder actuator pivot pin. This rationale is driven by marine steering rudder actuator pivot pin and fat life requirements.
process: Ring forging radial-axial for propulsion geometry
CNC turn-bore operation with SPC sampling
TIG welding autogenous with SPC sampling
Hydrostatic pressure test with SPC sampling
surfaceTreatment: Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater — tailored for marine steering rudder application
commonFailures: HE from over-protection below -0.85V vs Ag/AgCl - controlled by anode current density limiter circuit — critical for marine steering rudder performance

faq.q: What biofouling resistance does Titanium Submarine Steering Rudder Pin have?
faq.a: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V surfaces inhibit macrofouling attachment compared to steel due to the stable and chemically inert TiO₂ surface. For marine steering rudder in marine growth zones, the passive surface reduces barnacle adhesion strength by approximately 60% versus steel. Periodic mechanical cleaning does not accelerate corrosion as the passive film self-repairs in aerated seawater.
